claims.text: A two-step treatment consisting of ultra-rapid quenching followed by sub-Tg annealing will enhance amorphous retention and thermal stability in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Rapid quenching of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 produces an amorphous structure that is unstable and prone to crystallization during reheating.
Quenching Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 at 10^5–10^6 K/s will suppress crystallization and form an amorphous phase.
Annealing just below Tg promotes local structural relaxation in the quenched glass.
Sub-Tg annealing causes atomic rearrangements that transform a high-energy glass into a lower-energy glass state.
Sub-Tg annealing reduces internal stresses in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Sub-Tg annealing reduces the number of nucleation sites for crystallization.
A high cooling rate dynamically traps a high-energy amorphous state.
Low-temperature annealing can relax an amorphous structure without crystallizing it.
Structural relaxation lowers the thermodynamic driving force for crystallization during reheating.
The treatment will broaden the range of cooling rates that yield amorphous Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
The treated alloy will exhibit delayed or reduced crystallization during reheating.
The treated alloy will have a higher DSC crystallization-onset temperature than the unannealed alloy.
Cooling rate strongly affects transformation temperatures in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 forms an amorphous phase only at extreme cooling rates.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 displays a complicated, premature crystallization response during reheating.
If the cooling rate is too slow, the proposed treatment will not improve amorphous retention.
An annealing temperature that is too high can initiate unwanted crystallization.
Treatment success depends on annealing duration, with insufficient time giving inadequate relaxation and excessive treatment potentially causing crystallization.
The optimal sub-Tg annealing temperature and duration for this alloy are uncertain and require experimental optimization.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome claims a broader range of cooling rates that yields amorphous material, while the conditions and boundary state that ultra-rapid cooling is required and that compromised or slower cooling may yield no improvement.
